Subject: Integrate Health - Benchmark handoff & evidence digest

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our runbook, we completed the acceptance run on the dedicated staging pool this morning and I wanted to share the handoff summary and next steps so your SREs have a single place to pick up artifacts and context.

TL;DR
- Throughput target: 1200 req/s sustained at p95 latency <= 220ms for inference-only text-generation (max sequence 1024).
- Observed (after KV warmup & prefix caching): 1,350 req/s sustained; p95=198ms; tail spikes during garbage-collection windows capped at ~420ms.
- Small set of follow-ups: one retry pattern during burst ramps (we captured traces), and an environment knob we recommend for autoscaler headroom.

What I attached / linked:
- loadscript-integ-20270821.json — the exact load script we executed (concurrency stages + ramp durations).
- latency-summary-20270821.csv — p50/p95/p99 slices across stages and model variants.
- kv-warmup-log.txt — start-to-ready timing for KV cache priming on the pool.
- run-screencap-20270821.mp4 — short recording of the dashboard during the high-rpm stage.
- Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/INT-2027-0543/benchmark-artifacts

Key notes for your team (Integrate Health ops):
1) The fastest steady-state we observed used the quantized LlamaX-8q variant we provisioned — if you want lower latency at the same throughput, we can try the 4-bit profile but you'll trade off a small quality delta.
2) The autoscaler default cadence caused a brief underprovision during the 8x concurrency step; we suggested a 30s faster scale-out window to avoid the small retry cluster we saw.
3) We warmed the KV cache for 22 minutes — traffic characteristics you ship to prod will influence this. If you prefer cold-starts, we can rerun the script that simulates cold prefix churn.

Next steps / asks
- Can your team confirm whether Integrate Health wants the 4-bit experiment to reduce latency (we'll run comparative evidence)?
- Please confirm a window to hand the artifacts into your staging cluster so you can validate the same run in your VPC (we recommended 48-72h after this handoff).
- Let us know whether you want the autoscaler cadence change applied to your Dedicated config or whether you'll maintain the default and monitor.

I copied Monica (CS lead) and Karthik (performance eng) who will help with the follow-ups and run any additional proof-of-concept variants.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Onboarding Manager
Redwood Inference

I can confirm a window for us to validate in our staging VPC on Monday 2027-08-23 09:00 PT. Ops will be available.

Thanks — will loop in ops if any config approvals are necessary.

Sam —

Thanks for the quick review and for Monday's validation window. Couple of clarifications and the requested config diff below.

1) GC tail spikes: we instrumented both the model process and the runtime. The traces show short-lived CPU-side GC pauses from the model server bookkeeping thread (checkpoint pruning during high concurrency). The GPU driver latency remained flat. Mitigation options:
   - Short term: stagger the background prune to run between ramp stages (we included a small patch in the runbook to avoid prune during the 8x step).
   - Mid term: we can push a minor model-server patch that avoids synchronous pruning while token emission is ongoing.

2) Autoscaler diff (applies to Dedicated profile INT-2027-0543):
   - current: scale_out_window = 90s; cool_down = 180s
   - suggested: scale_out_window = 60s; cool_down = 120s
We will apply this for the Monday run, monitor tail latencies, and revert if you see instability. I attached a one-line patch below to apply server-side via your infra repo.

3) 4-bit experiment: sounds good to run at 10% shadow traffic first. Karthik will coordinate the rollout and produce a short A/B quality snapshot (perplexity + a small set of golden prompts you provided).

Logistics for Monday 2027-08-23 09:00 PT:
- Redwood on call: Monica (CS), Karthik (perf eng), and one runtime SRE.
- Integrate Health on call: Sam + ops.
- Acceptance checklist we'll run: cold-start ramp, steady-state 20m at target, burst-step validation, and KV durability check.

I'll drop the patch and the run checklist to the Drive folder now.

Cheers,
Monica Patel

Sam / team —

We're all set for the Monday window and I wanted to add a short results note you'll find useful when you validate in your VPC.

Observed artifacts and recommended check points:
- Warmed sequence: after ~22m the KV hit rate stabilized at 97.6% — expect a ~3–5% hit-rate degradation if you have heavy prefix churn.
- Tail analysis: p99 showed spikes correlated with concurrent heavy control-plane operations (snapshot flush). If you schedule the acceptance run, avoid snapshot windows (I marked them in the Drive calendar).
- Retry pattern: we logged a 0.6% transient retry rate during the 8x concurrency ramp — root cause is a short-lived 503 from the model side when GPU memory briefly hit a burst threshold. We mitigated on the fly by removing a low-priority background worker and the retry frequency dropped <0.1%.

What I'll run Monday during the shadow 4-bit experiment (10%):
1) Golden prompts (provided) against LlamaX-8q and LlamaX-4bit-shadow.
2) Compute quality delta (token-level edit + perplexity sample) and flag any prompts with >3% divergence for human review.
3) Smoke for stability: 10-min steady at 500 req/s to confirm tail behavior.

If you want to proceed after Monday, I'll prepare an evidence packet with per-variant perf tables and a short write-up you can store in your compliance folder.

See you Monday — I'll be on the call and will have the run logs streaming to the Drive folder.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
